# Gallery basics

## Quickstart

Build a responsive photo album with one module, one photo collection, and one
component. Each photo includes its intrinsic dimensions, so Nuxt Photo can
render useful geometry on the server before the image downloads.

::info{icon="lucide:package-check"}
If the project still uses `0.1.x`, follow the [0.2 upgrade guide](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/resources/upgrade-to-0-2)
before copying the examples;
collection ownership, layout options, and import paths changed.
::

## 1. Install the module

::code-group

```bash [npm]
npm install @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

```bash [bun]
bun add @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

```bash [deno]
deno add npm:@nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

::

Read the package manifest for the authoritative Nuxt and Node compatibility ranges.

## 2. Register it

Use the full theme for the first result. You can switch to structure-only CSS
when the gallery is working.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt-photo/nuxt'],
  nuxtPhoto: {
    css: 'all',
  },
})
```

The module registers `Photo`, `PhotoAlbum`, `PhotoGroup`, and `PhotoCarousel`.
It also auto-imports `useLightbox`, `useLightboxProvider`, and `responsive`.

## 3. Render the album

```vue [app/pages/index.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { PhotoItem } from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'

const photos: PhotoItem[] = [
  {
    id: 'desert',
    src: '/photos/desert.jpg',
    width: 1280,
    height: 800,
    alt: 'Sand dunes at golden hour',
    caption: 'Desert light',
  },
  {
    id: 'coast',
    src: '/photos/coast.jpg',
    width: 960,
    height: 1200,
    alt: 'Rocky coast seen from above',
    caption: 'From above',
  },
  {
    id: 'forest',
    src: '/photos/forest.jpg',
    width: 1200,
    height: 800,
    alt: 'Morning mist between pine trees',
    caption: 'Forest haze',
  },
]
</script>

<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :layout="{ type: 'rows', targetRowHeight: 240 }" />
</template>
```

Put matching files in `public/photos`, start the app, and select a thumbnail.
The album opens its lightbox by default. Use the arrow keys to navigate and
`Escape` to close it.

## Use real image data

Every item needs a stable string `id`, a `src`, and finite positive `width` and
`height`. The dimensions must match the source image. Invalid data throws at
the component boundary instead of producing an unstable layout.

If the data comes from a CMS, map it to `PhotoItem` once in the loader or
composable. The [CMS gallery guide](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/guides/cms-gallery) keeps that mapping
out of the template, while [the photo model](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/concepts/photo-model)
documents validation and optional fields.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/1.getting-started/1.index.md`_

## Installation

Nuxt apps install `@nuxt-photo/nuxt`. The Vue package is already a dependency,
so app code can use auto-imports or import explicitly from
`@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app`.

## Requirements

The package manifests are the source of truth for supported Nuxt, Node, Vue,
and optional Nuxt Image ranges. Your package manager reports an actionable peer
error when an application falls outside them.

## Add the module

Nuxt can install and register it in one command:

```bash [Terminal]
npx nuxi module add @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

For a manual setup, install the package and add it to `modules`:

::code-group

```bash [npm]
npm install @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

```bash [bun]
bun add @nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

```bash [deno]
deno add npm:@nuxt-photo/nuxt
```

::

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt-photo/nuxt'],
})
```

The default `css: 'structure'` loads the geometry required by albums,
carousels, photos, and the lightbox without applying the complete visual theme.
Use `css: 'all'` while evaluating the library or when the default theme fits
the project.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt-photo/nuxt'],
  nuxtPhoto: {
    css: 'all',
  },
})
```

## Add Nuxt Image

Install `@nuxt/image` only when thumbnails and slides should use its providers
and responsive image generation.

::code-group

```bash [npm]
npm install @nuxt/image
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @nuxt/image
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @nuxt/image
```

```bash [bun]
bun add @nuxt/image
```

```bash [deno]
deno add npm:@nuxt/image
```

::

Register it in the same modules list. In the default `image.provider: 'auto'`
mode, Nuxt Photo detects the registered module after module installation and
uses it. Without `@nuxt/image`, it uses the native adapter.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt-photo/nuxt', '@nuxt/image'],
  image: {
    domains: ['images.example.com'],
  },
})
```

## Explore the module options

Choose the CSS layer, image provider, registered components, auto-imports, and
lightbox minimum zoom. The generated configuration shows which changes require
an app restart.

Use the [module configuration reference](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/reference/configuration) to
change component prefixes, primitive registration, CSS ownership, image
defaults, or the global minimum zoom.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/1.getting-started/2.installation.md`_

## How Nuxt Photo works

Nuxt Photo separates photo data from the way that data is laid out, delivered, and opened. Every built-in experience starts with the same `PhotoItem` collection and adds only the behavior it owns.

```text [Architecture]
PhotoItem[]
    |
    +-- recipe component ---- layout and triggers
    +-- image adapter ------- final image attributes
    +-- lightbox provider --- navigation, zoom, gestures, and focus
```

## Start with a recipe component

Recipe components cover the common paths without exposing the underlying state model.

| Component         | Use it for                                                  | Lightbox default |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `<Photo>`         | One figure, with an optional solo viewer                    | Off              |
| `<PhotoAlbum>`    | Rows, columns, or masonry                                   | On               |
| `<PhotoGroup>`    | One viewer shared by several descendant recipes             | On               |
| `<PhotoCarousel>` | A horizontal carousel with optional thumbnails and controls | Off              |

`PhotoAlbum` is the usual starting point. It validates the collection, calculates the selected layout, renders image triggers, and creates its own lightbox provider.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" layout="rows" />
</template>
```

The [component reference](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/components/photo-album) lists the props and slots when the default recipe already matches the intended structure.

## Share a collection deliberately

Each standalone recipe with a lightbox enabled owns its own viewer. Wrap related recipes in `PhotoGroup` when they should navigate through one ordered collection instead.

```vue [app/pages/portfolio.vue]
<template>
  <PhotoGroup :photos="allPhotos">
    <PhotoAlbum :photos="landscapes" />
    <PhotoAlbum :photos="portraits" />
  </PhotoGroup>
</template>
```

The group collection is canonical. Descendant order can change without changing the lightbox order, and every descendant ID must exist in the group collection.

## Move down one layer at a time

Use the narrowest customization surface that produces the required result:

1. Change recipe props for layout, behavior, and classes.
2. Replace a recipe slot for custom thumbnail, caption, control, or slide markup.
3. Combine `LightboxProvider`, `PhotoTrigger`, and the recipe `Lightbox` for a custom thumbnail layout.
4. Compose the lightbox primitives when the overlay, viewport, controls, or caption structure must change.

The lower layers preserve Nuxt Photo's state and interaction model, but they give the application more responsibility for markup, styling, and accessibility. The [custom thumbnail guide](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/customization/custom-thumbnail-layout) shows the provider boundary without rebuilding the viewer.

## Keep each setting at its owner

Module options choose app-wide registration, CSS, image delivery, and lightbox defaults. Recipe props configure one rendered experience. `PhotoItem` carries content data, while slots and primitives own custom markup.

Keeping those boundaries intact prevents duplicated providers, competing navigation order, and image behavior that differs between thumbnails and slides.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/2.concepts/1.how-it-works.md`_

## Photo model

Every Nuxt Photo component consumes `PhotoItem`. Normalize CMS records, API responses, and local assets to this shape before rendering them.

```ts [app/data/photos.ts]
import type { PhotoItem } from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'

export const photos: PhotoItem[] = [
  {
    id: 'alpine-lake',
    src: '/photos/alpine-lake.jpg',
    thumbSrc: '/photos/alpine-lake-thumb.jpg',
    width: 1600,
    height: 1000,
    alt: 'An alpine lake below a rocky ridge',
    caption: 'Alpine lake',
  },
]
```

## Required fields

| Field    | Requirement                                | Why it matters                                               |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`     | Non-empty string, unique in the collection | Preserves active-photo identity and trigger registration     |
| `src`    | Non-empty string                           | Supplies the full image source                               |
| `width`  | Positive finite number                     | Reserves the correct aspect ratio and drives layout geometry |
| `height` | Positive finite number                     | Reserves the correct aspect ratio and drives layout geometry |

Use intrinsic pixel dimensions, not the rendered CSS size. Incorrect dimensions produce incorrect album geometry and an inaccurate opening frame even when the browser can still load the image.

Use an asset or CMS identifier for `id`. Array indexes change when a list is filtered or reordered and therefore cannot preserve identity reliably.

## Optional fields

| Field         | Behavior                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `alt`         | Becomes the image alternative text; an omitted value renders as an empty string |
| `caption`     | Appears in the `Photo` figure and the default lightbox                          |
| `description` | Adds longer text to the default lightbox caption                                |
| `thumbSrc`    | Replaces `src` for thumbnails in the native image path                          |
| `srcset`      | Passes explicit candidates to the native image path                             |
| `meta`        | Carries application-owned data into slots and adapters                          |

Keep `meta` for presentation data that Nuxt Photo does not interpret, such as a photographer, credit URL, or media kind.

```ts [app/data/photos.ts]
type PhotoMeta = {
  photographer: string
  creditUrl: string
}

export const photos: PhotoItem<PhotoMeta>[] = [
  {
    id: 'alpine-lake',
    src: '/photos/alpine-lake.jpg',
    width: 1600,
    height: 1000,
    meta: {
      photographer: 'Ada Example',
      creditUrl: 'https://example.com/ada',
    },
  },
]
```

## Validation fails at the rendering boundary

`Photo` and `PhotoGroup` reject invalid data. `PhotoAlbum` and `PhotoCarousel` also default to `validation="throw"`, which raises a `PhotoValidationError` before layout calculation.

Use `validation="drop"` only when omitting invalid entries is an intentional product decision. Handle the `invalidPhotos` event so a broken CMS response remains visible. The event is client-only and runs after rendering; report server-side ingestion failures at the data boundary instead.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { InvalidPhotosEvent } from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'

function reportInvalidPhotos(event: InvalidPhotosEvent) {
  console.error('Invalid photo collection', event.issues)
}
</script>

<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" validation="drop" @invalid-photos="reportInvalidPhotos" />
</template>
```

Map external records once at the application boundary. The [CMS gallery guide](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/guides/cms-gallery) keeps source-specific fields out of component templates.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/2.concepts/2.photo-model.md`_

## PhotoAlbum

`<PhotoAlbum>` is the default gallery recipe. It validates the collection, computes layout from intrinsic dimensions, and enables its own lightbox unless a parent group owns one.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { responsive, type PhotoItem } from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'

const { data: response } = await useFetch<PhotoItem[]>('/api/photos')
const photos = computed(() => response.value ?? [])
const spacing = responsive({ 0: 4, 640: 8, 1024: 12 })
</script>

<template>
  <PhotoAlbum
    :photos="photos"
    :layout="{ type: 'rows', targetRowHeight: responsive({ 0: 160, 720: 260 }) }"
    :spacing="spacing"
  />
</template>
```

## Props

| Prop                    | Type                                              | Default                | Purpose                                                |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `photos`                | `readonly PhotoItem[]`                            | required               | Collection to validate and lay out                     |
| `validation`            | `'throw' \| 'drop'`                               | `'throw'`              | Controls invalid-photo handling                        |
| `invalidPhotos` event   | `(event: InvalidPhotosEvent) => void`             | none                   | Reports dropped invalid entries after client rendering |
| `layout`                | `AlbumLayout \| 'rows' \| 'columns' \| 'masonry'` | `'rows'`               | Selects the algorithm and its options                  |
| `spacing`               | `ResponsiveParameter<number>`                     | `8`                    | Gap between items in pixels                            |
| `padding`               | `ResponsiveParameter<number>`                     | `0`                    | Padding around each item in pixels                     |
| `defaultContainerWidth` | `number`                                          | none                   | Seeds deterministic server layout                      |
| `breakpoints`           | `readonly number[]`                               | inferred when possible | Snaps measured client width                            |
| `sizes`                 | rows sizes object                                 | none                   | Computes the image `sizes` attribute for measured rows |
| `imageAdapter`          | `ImageAdapter`                                    | injected, then native  | Overrides image delivery                               |
| `lightbox`              | `boolean \| Component`                            | `true`                 | Enables, disables, or replaces the viewer              |
| `transition`            | `LightboxTransitionOption`                        | `'auto'`               | Configures viewer motion                               |
| `itemClass`             | `string`                                          | none                   | Adds classes to each item wrapper                      |
| `imgClass`              | `string`                                          | none                   | Adds classes to each default image                     |

## Layout values

Rows target `300px` by default. Columns and masonry use `3` columns by default.

```vue [app/components/PhotoLayouts.vue]
<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :layout="{ type: 'rows', targetRowHeight: 240 }" />
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :layout="{ type: 'columns', columns: 3 }" />
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :layout="{ type: 'masonry', columns: 4 }" />
</template>
```

Columns preserve source order within balanced sequential columns. Masonry assigns each next item to the shortest column, so its visual and DOM reading order differs from a simple row sequence.

An explicit non-empty `breakpoints` array replaces inferred `responsive()` breakpoints rather than merging with them. Below the smallest positive breakpoint, the observer keeps the real width.

## Server rendering

Rows render a complete flex fallback without an assumed width. Columns and masonry render a simple grid fallback, then form measured groups after mount. Set a positive `defaultContainerWidth` when server and client should start with the same grouping.

The `sizes` prop is specific to rows. It is computed for measured rows; the container-query branch used without `defaultContainerWidth` does not add a computed `sizes` value.

## Thumbnail slot

`thumbnail` receives `{ photo, index, width, height, hidden }`. It replaces the default `<PhotoImage>`, so render that primitive inside the slot when custom markup should retain the configured adapter.

```vue [app/components/LabeledAlbum.vue]
<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos">
    <template #thumbnail="{ photo, hidden }">
      <figure :style="{ opacity: hidden ? 0 : 1 }">
        <PhotoImage :photo="photo" context="thumb" />
        <figcaption>{{ photo.caption }}</figcaption>
      </figure>
    </template>
  </PhotoAlbum>
</template>
```

Inside an enabled `<PhotoGroup>`, the album registers thumbnails with that group and does not create another lightbox. A disabled parent group makes descendant albums inert. Treat `lightbox` and `transition` as setup-time provider choices; photos, layout inputs, `sizes`, and `imageAdapter` remain reactive.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/7.components/2.photo-album.md`_
